A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniCombine and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material. Existing content can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments in Table 1, ablations and computational measurements in Tables 2–5, and additional experimental results in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds qualitative experiments with increasing numbers of conditions and reference-style control in Figures 12–13.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same LoRA Switching, CMMDiT attention, and Denoising-LoRA procedures. The StyleBooth application trains another instance of the existing Condition-LoRA component; no architectural, loss, or inference-rule change is documented.

E1.justification: V2 adds StyleBooth as training data for reference-style conditioning and demonstrates Spatial-Style generation. Figure 12 also extends evaluated input combinations to subject, background, depth, and Canny together. These are limited extensions of the retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains UniControl/UniControlNet, ObjectStitch/AnyDoor, and ControlNet with IP-Adapter/Ctrl-X in their corresponding comparisons. Table 5 also retains its comparators. The new figures compare conditioning configurations without introducing another competing method.

E3.justification: New qualitative comparisons progressively combine one through four conditions in Figure 12 and compare generation without style conditioning against three reference styles in Figure 13. Existing metrics, training settings, and Appendix A1 dataset partitions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 12 adds a qualitative analysis of control as conditional branches increase, while Figure 13 adds a stylization case study. Existing attention, LoRA-placement, and training-block ablations, including Appendix A2, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added demonstrations introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–5 and A1–A3 are unchanged. Figures 12–13 add qualitative results for additional condition combinations and reference styles; they do not report improved scores under the original evaluation settings.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow objective, sequence and attention definitions in Equations 1–5, and quadratic-to-linear attention-complexity argument are unchanged. V2 adds no mathematical derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about general conditional combination, SubjectSpatial200K, and state-of-the-art performance. The new demonstrations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets increasing conditional branches as providing finer control and explains reference-style applicability through training a Condition-LoRA. These additions extend the discussion of practical extensibility; existing mechanism explanations and training-free failure discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 identifies training a new Condition-LoRA on StyleBooth as preparation for Spatial-Style generation. This adds limited implementation information, but no adapter-specific training budget or hyperparameters. Existing implementation details, partitioning instructions, and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the StyleBooth citation to identify the new adapter's training source. The other 60 references and related-work positioning are retained; their citation-number changes are purely editorial.

P1.justification: V2 adds two short passages, 'More Conditional Branches' and 'More Application Scenarios,' after the existing ablation discussion. It also updates affiliation and corresponding-author information. The remaining narrative and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 inserts two qualitative figure grids, Figures 12–13, on page 9, moving the conclusion downward and reflowing references. Existing figures, tables, and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Figures 12–13 provide concrete visual support for combining more conditions and extending control to reference styles, modestly strengthening evidence for the framework's generality. The original results and appendices are preserved. The gain remains limited because the additions are illustrative cases without quantitative evaluation or a detailed recipe for training the new style adapter.
